about: Featured paths for the walkthrough (python -m musichistory paths). Each path is a work_id sequence whose consecutive songs are joined by an identity-lineage edge (earlier -> later) and all have a preview; the stage checks the rules and skips a path that breaks them. Titles and descriptions are hand-written and describe the music only. Edit freely, then rerun the stage.

paths.name: Four Chords Worldwide
paths.title: Four chords, three styles
paths.description: Reggae, British pop and Latin pop built on the same I–V–vi–IV loop, the 'axis' progression; the chord check hears it in all three previews.

paths.name: The Axis Loop
paths.title: The axis loop, 1983–2018
paths.description: The I–V–vi–IV loop carried through four decades of ballads: Cyndi Lauper's lilting 1983 hit, Lonestar's country-pop, John Legend's piano ballad and Lewis Capaldi.

paths.name: Doo-Wop Changes
paths.title: Doo-wop changes
paths.description: The I–vi–IV–V progression of 1950s doo-wop, carried from Paul Anka's teen pop to Coldplay's string-driven 2008 hit; the chord check hears it in every preview.

paths.name: Rock and Roll Twelve Bars
paths.title: Rock 'n' roll twelve bars
paths.description: The 12-bar blues form under four early rock 'n' roll records, from Carl Perkins's rockabilly and Buddy Holly to Ray Charles and Dion.

paths.name: Aeolian Rock
paths.title: Minor-key rock: i–bVI–bVII
paths.description: The Aeolian i–bVI–bVII move of Layla's riff, passed on to Fleetwood Mac's Go Your Own Way and Prince's Little Red Corvette.

paths.name: Orbison to Flowers
paths.title: Orbison to Flowers
paths.description: Only the Lonely shares an exact bass riff with Duke of Earl; from there the I–vi–ii–V turnaround runs through Oh, Pretty Woman to Miley Cyrus's Flowers.

paths.name: Summer Place to Barbie Girl
paths.title: A Summer Place to Barbie Girl
paths.description: The I–vi–ii–V turnaround, from Percy Faith's 1959 string theme through Redbone's Come and Get Your Love to Aqua's Barbie Girl.

paths.name: Every Breath, Interpolated
paths.title: Every Breath You Take, interpolated
paths.description: A two-chord drift from 1967 leads into the Police's 1983 arpeggiated guitar figure, which came back note for note in 1997 as the backbone of a Puff Daddy and Faith Evans tribute.

paths.name: Banana Boat to Dynamite
paths.title: Day-O to Dynamite, 1956–2010
paths.description: A calypso I–vi–V loop leads from Harry Belafonte's Day-O to Fine Young Cannibals, whose 24-note bass figure turns up again in Taio Cruz's Dynamite.

paths.name: Stairway to Let Her Go
paths.title: Stairway to Heaven to Let Her Go
paths.description: The I–V–vi move of Stairway to Heaven reaches Avril Lavigne's Complicated, whose Aeolian i–bVI–bVII turn carries on into Passenger's Let Her Go.

paths.name: Hung Up to Love Story
paths.title: Hung Up to Love Story, 2005–2008
paths.description: Three years of 2000s pop on one four-chord cycle: Madonna's vi–IV–I–iii dance loop, Rihanna's Umbrella and Taylor Swift's Love Story, which share the I–V–vi–IV axis.

paths.name: Stand by Me to Basket Case
paths.title: Stand by Me to Basket Case
paths.description: The three-chord I–IV–V framework, from Ben E. King's 1961 soul ballad through Band Aid's 1984 charity single to Green Day's punk.

paths.name: U2 to the Chili Peppers
paths.title: With or Without You to Dani California
paths.description: U2's I–V–vi–IV loop is shared by Madonna's Like a Prayer, whose vi–V–ii turn leads on to the Red Hot Chili Peppers' Dani California.

paths.name: Platters to Shania
paths.title: The Great Pretender to Still the One
paths.description: The I–IV–V changes, from the Platters' 1955 ballad through the Beatles' Please Please Me to Shania Twain's 1997 country-pop.

paths.name: Beat It to Party Rock
paths.title: Beat It to Party Rock Anthem
paths.description: Minor-key rock and dance on the i–bVII shuttle: Michael Jackson's Beat It, 3 Doors Down's Here Without You and its Aeolian i–bVI–bVII, carried into LMFAO's Party Rock Anthem.

paths.name: Managua to George Jones
paths.title: Managua, Nicaragua to George Jones
paths.description: A 1946 big-band ii–V–I cadence leads to Elvis Presley's It's Now or Never, whose I–IV–V changes run on to George Jones's 1980 country ballad.
